title: High-efficiency S. cerevisiae lithium acetate transformation
author: Carl De Boer
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j4tcqwn

steps.title: Inoculate starter culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate 5 mL YPD medium and grow overnight (or scale up as appropriate).

steps.title: Dilute and grow to target OD
steps.instruction: In the morning, dilute the overnight culture into approximately 100 mL fresh YPD to an initial OD₆₀₀ of ~0.05. Grow 4–6 h until OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.3–0.4; scale up the starting culture as needed for the number of transformations.

steps.title: Prepare reagents on ice
steps.instruction: Place the following solutions on ice: 50 % (w/v) PEG 3350, 1 M lithium acetate (LiAc), 0.1 M LiAc, and sterile water.

steps.title: Denature ssDNA
steps.instruction: Prepare single‑stranded DNA at 2 mg/mL, heat to 100 °C for 5 min, snap‑cool on ice, and keep on ice until used in the transformation.

steps.title: Harvest cells
steps.instruction: When the culture reaches the desired OD, collect cells by centrifugation at 3000 rpm for 5 min.

steps.title: Keep cells on ice
steps.instruction: From this point until the 30 °C incubation step, keep the cell pellet on ice.

steps.title: First wash with water
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL ice‑cold H₂O, transfer to an Eppendorf tube (scale volume proportionally for larger cultures), and centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 2 min.

steps.title: Second wash and optional freezing
steps.instruction: Wash cells once with 0.5 mL ice‑cold 0.1 M LiAc and centrifuge as before. Optional: resuspend in 0.1 M LiAc, add glycerol to a final concentration of 15 % (v/v), and freeze at –80 °C. For later use, thaw on ice, repeat the wash, and continue the protocol.

steps.title: Resuspend in minimal water
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed pellet in as little ice‑cold H₂O as possible (≈100 µL for a 200 mL starting culture; adjust as needed) by pipetting up and down until a thick suspension is obtained.

steps.title: Assemble transformation mixture
steps.instruction: On ice, prepare a 214 µL transformation mixture (excluding plasmid DNA) as follows: 30 µL denatured ssDNA (2 mg/mL), 140 µL 50 % PEG 3350, 22 µL 1 M LiAc, 2.12 µL 1 M DTT, and 1–2 µL plasmid DNA (~2 µg/µL). Vortex well, add 20 µL of the cell suspension, and vortex gently until homogeneous. (Plasmid DNA may also be added after the cell addition and vortexed again.)

steps.title: Incubate at 30 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the transformation mixture at 30 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Heat‑shock at 42 °C
steps.instruction: Heat‑shock the mixture at 42 °C for 20 min.

steps.title: Brief centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge briefly (≈30 s, low rpm; <1 min) to pellet cells; a mini‑centrifuge is sufficient.

steps.title: Resuspend for recovery or plating
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in the desired volume of H₂O or selective medium. If plating on an antibiotic, allow up to 2 h recovery in non‑selective medium before plating (recovery improves colony numbers).

steps.title: Plate dilution series
steps.instruction: Plate appropriate dilutions (e.g., 10⁻⁴) on selective agar and incubate ~2 days for colony development.

steps.title: Grow library in selective media
steps.instruction: If maintaining a library, grow cells in selective medium for 1–2 days, diluting at least once to keep selection pressure. Use a volume proportional to the number of transformed cells (e.g., ≥50 mL selective medium for cells derived from a 50 mL starter culture).
